title: Edmund and the Orchard
premise: In the aftermath of a civil war, Paloma Whitlock completes her dead master's atlas of contested borderlands, only to receive a letter in his unmistakable hand — from a man officially executed twenty years ago. Following the handwriting to a hidden orchard where survivors of a massacred village have lived in silence, she discovers her master faked his death to protect them and the true map that proves the victors stole the land. As government historians close in to canonize their version, Paloma must choose between the safety of silence she was taught and publishing the truth, knowing it will destroy her guild standing. She smuggles the atlas's true plates out through an old smuggling route, publishes them abroad, and returns to find the orchard burned but its people scattered into witness — the record finally on paper, even as the victors' history hardens around them.
about_author: Noor Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced communities' land records before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about documents, memory, and the people history forgets to ask.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Coastline
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Twenty years after Master Aldous Whitlock's execution, Paloma inks the final coastline of his atlas in the guild workshop, hiding her grief in precision. When the guild announces the atlas will be 'corrected' by official historians, she feels the silences she has kept pressing against her ribs. Beat: dutiful unease.

chapters.title: A Letter in a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A stranger named Ivo Reyes arrives at her door carrying a letter whose flourished capitals she would know anywhere: Aldous's hand. The letter names an orchard and begs her to bring the atlas's original plates before the historians' commission arrives. Beat: vertigo — the dead do not write.

chapters.title: What the Guild Keeps
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Searching the guild archives for Aldous's trial records, she finds pages razored out and a seal she doesn't recognize on the replacement folios. Her mentor, Provost Halloway, warns her gently off — too gently. Beat: first crack in the safe world of rules.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Cargo
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo reveals he is the son of villagers from Merrow Fen, a town erased from every map, and that he has spent years finding anyone left who could read Aldous's cipher. He doesn't fully trust Paloma; she was trained by the guild that condemned him. Beat: wary alliance forged under mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: North by Smugglers' Light
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Fleeing the city ahead of guild messengers, Paloma and Ivo travel the old salt routes she once mapped from rumor rather than survey. She realizes Aldous taught her those routes deliberately, like a message stored in her own memory. Beat: the apprenticeship reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Orchard at World's Edge
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They reach a terraced orchard above a drowned valley where forty survivors of Merrow Fen live unrecorded, growing apples from trees carried out of the burning town. An old woman, Sera Voss, greets Paloma by her childhood nickname — Aldous wrote to them about her. Beat: belonging offered like a wound reopened.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Sera Voss's POV. Sera recounts the massacre night: how Aldous, then the army's chief cartographer, refused to map the town for artillery and instead led families out through fog he invented on the chart. His 'execution' was staged; his silence was the price of theirs. Beat: grief transfigured into awe.

chapters.title: The True Plates
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In a root cellar, Aldous — older, half-blind, furious that Ivo found him — shows her the real atlas: surveys proving Merrow Fen stood on land granted to the villagers by charter, land the victorious Duke claimed empty. He never sent for her because her safety depended on ignorance. Beat: love expressed as abandonment, understood at last.

chapters.title: Arguments in the Press House
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Aldous argues the plates must burn with him; a published truth gets people hanged, as his co-conspirator was. Paloma counters that unpublished truth dies twice — once in fire, once in the historians' ink. The orchard votes, badly split. Beat: the book's moral argument made flesh.

chapters.title: Commission
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Word arrives that the Royal Historical Commission will pass through the valley within the fortnight, 'surveying' what remains of Merrow Fen to certify the Duke's title. Among the commissioners: Provost Halloway, who razored the archive pages. Beat: the clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Halloway's Bargain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Halloway, arriving early under a flag of scholarship, privately offers Paloma restoration of her guild standing if she surrenders the plates — revealing he helped stage Aldous's death out of guilt and has protected the secret ever since. Protection, he says, requires the past stay buried. Beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Night the Apples Fell
chapters.summary: Sera Voss's POV. A storm flattens half the orchard the same night someone marks the cellar entrance for the commission. Suspicion falls on a young orchard keeper, Tam, whose brother serves the Duke. Sera refuses to let fear make them into the people who burned them. Beat: community tested from inside.

chapters.title: Tam's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam confesses he wrote to his brother years ago, not betraying the orchard but begging for news — and his letters were read. He offers to carry false word to the commission as penance. The vote shifts: the truth will go out, but it needs a route and a decoy. Beat: guilt converted into purpose.

chapters.title: Copying the Truth
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Working by lamplight, Paloma copies the true plates while Aldous dictates corrections his failing eyes can no longer draw, their hands overlapping on the same vellum across twenty lost years. She hides one full set inside the binding of her own apprentice atlas. Beat: reconciliation enacted through craft.

chapters.title: The Decoy Atlas
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo and Tam prepare a convincing forgery — beautiful, wrong, and damning if seized — to feed the commission. Ivo admits to Paloma that his search for Aldous began as revenge for his father and became something else; he asks her what she'll do when the record exists and no one may be allowed to read it. Beat: stakes sharpened beyond survival.

chapters.title: The Commission Comes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The commission arrives with soldiers; Halloway performs a scholarly inspection while a captain searches the terraces. Paloma, presenting herself as guild escort, walks the officers through ruins she has secretly re-mapped, narrating erasure so fluently they never suspect the guide. Beat: tension sustained through performance.

chapters.title: Aldous Steps Forward
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. The captain produces a wanted poster; a soldier recognizes Aldous despite the years. Rather than let the orchard be searched house by house, Aldous surrenders himself, claiming the plates are his alone and buried where only he knows. Beat: the master spends his last currency buying time.

chapters.title: The Salt Road at Night
chapters.summary: Paloma and Ivo's alternating POV. While Aldous stalls the commission with a fabricated dig site, Paloma and Ivo carry the true plates down the flooded salt road by night, nearly drowning when a culvert collapses. Ivo takes the second set, splitting the risk so no single capture kills the truth. Beat: climax of endurance and sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Halloway Saw
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Left alone with the captured Aldous, Halloway finds the decoy atlas, understands the whole design, and must choose: expose it and undo his twenty years of guilty protection, or let the prisoners escape and fall himself. He burns the commission's seizure order and unlocks the cell. Beat: the antagonist's conscience becomes the hinge of the plot.

chapters.title: The Burning Orchard
chapters.summary: Sera Voss's POV. Retaliating for the fiasco, soldiers torch the orchard; the survivors scatter along routes Paloma mapped for exactly this day. Sera stays until the last family is gone, then walks out carrying a sapling from the oldest tree. Beat: devastating loss transformed into diaspora of witnesses.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In a free port across the strait, Paloma and Ivo publish the true atlas with sworn testimonies from eleven surviving villagers, including Aldous's confession of the falsified execution order. Aldous did not survive the escape; his last letter to Paloma tells her the atlas was always hers to finish. Beat: catharsis — grief and triumph in one breath.

chapters.title: The New Margins
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A year later, banned in the Duchy but copied widely abroad, the atlas forces an inquiry the victors cannot fully smother. Paloma teaches apprentices in exile, planting Sera's sapling outside her schoolroom, and begins a new map — this time drawing the silences in, not out. Beat: inheritance fulfilled; memory given a place to grow.
